# Normalized document validators

The native document profile implements the original closed RecordRuleValidator vocabulary: length, pattern, min/max, one_of, email, URL, UUID, integer and decimal. Malformed arguments produce ordered `validator_invalid` findings when the original rule actually evaluates its argument; short-circuited non-string candidates retain the ordinary rule finding. Null/required/nullable handling precedes validators. UTF-8 strings count Unicode code points, not bytes or grapheme clusters.

Normalized ExactDecimal values use the explicit object `{"type":"exact-decimal","value":"12.30"}`. A plain string remains a string. Tagged literals must already be canonical, fixed-scale base-10 values within 65 digits; input tags are not constructors or a codec. The document layer retains this kind for validators, exposes scalar strings to expressions, and returns canonical scalar strings. Optional field `type`, `precision`, `scale`, `length` and `normalizers` metadata controls normalization of declared decimal range bounds through the existing exact-decimal kernel. `one_of` compares the canonical scalar strictly.

Patterns use PHP's wrapping and UTF/UCP/NEVER_BACKSLASH_C/DOLLAR_ENDONLY flags with explicit 100,000-match/1,000-depth limits. Engine statically embeds maintained PCRE2 10.42 and the complete pinned SLJIT source closure, matching the oracle's PCRE2 grammar version. JIT compilation uses PCRE2_JIT_COMPLETE and each match has PHP's bounded 32–192 KiB JIT stack. A pattern not accepted by JIT runs through PCRE2's interpreter, as PHP does; JIT execution failures remain validator failures. The 128-case edge corpus includes the observed Unicode-backslash-C and 600/2,000-level recursive-pattern regressions. The dependency is the narrow reviewed exception to the standard-library-only ceiling; no system PCRE, runtime loader or network source retrieval is used.

PCRE2 comes from upstream `release/pcre2-10.42` commit `26eb5f6712f2d2e6d3d012b273c53f7b4d420379`, based on release tag commit `52c08847921a324c804cabf2814549f50bce1265`. All eight security/high-severity backports recommended by upstream SUPPORT-LIFECYCLE as checked on 2026-09-07 are included. `resources/pcre2-source.json` lists every selected unmodified source digest and the exact commit/digest of each retained upstream patch. CMake verifies this source closure before compilation; sanitizer and fuzz builds instrument it. Recheck upstream lifecycle/advisories for every release candidate. There is no claim that a source lock replaces future security maintenance.

The email regexp is the default non-Unicode FILTER_VALIDATE_EMAIL expression from PHP 8.5, with its Michael Rushton attribution retained. The PHP license is distributed alongside PCRE2's license. URL validation reproduces the existing http/https restriction and parse_url/FILTER_VALIDATE_URL details; UUID validation preserves Ramsey GenericValidator's exact token-removal behavior, including brace/URN forms.

Current values and findings are charged against the whole-document output budget before insertion. Computed fields cannot accumulate hundreds of copies and only fail at final encoding. The final exact JSON encoding remains a second bound.

Host-normalized domain values additionally use `{"type":"normalized-value","version":1,"kind":KIND,"value":PAYLOAD}`. Kinds `money`, `quantity`, `zoned-datetime`, `datetime` and `encrypted` carry the owner's canonical storage payload. This is admission of an already normalized value, never currency conversion, timezone resolution, secret sealing or caller-object execution. Expressions see canonical ISO strings for dates and null for money, quantities, encrypted values and arrays. Validators retain original runtime kind, so a date object cannot pass a string validator merely because its storage spelling is a string. Final `values` are canonical storage values.

The `array` kind preserves PHP insertion order and key types using payload `{"entries":[{"key":KEY,"value":NORMALIZED_VALUE},...]}`. Integer-looking PHP keys must already be integers; duplicate keys are refused. Canonical output sorts maps and preserves lists, while immutable comparisons use ordered entries and recursively compare explicit domain-instance provenance. Plain JSON lists/maps are admitted as portable arrays, with map keys in JSON parser order; hosts must send ordered tags whenever original PHP insertion order matters. Structural admission is bounded to eight levels and 4,096 semantic nodes per field. Reserved tag-shaped maps can be represented unambiguously inside an ordered array tag.

A domain tag may additionally carry `instance`, a positive integer assigned from one host `SplObjectStorage` (or equivalent actual identity map) for this input document/correlation within one execution. Repeated tokens must have the same domain kind and canonical payload; conflicting reuse inside that input document refuses the entire batch as invalid input. The same token proves the same supplied source instance, distinct tokens prove different source instances. When equal-looking domain objects require strict identity but either token is absent, execution refuses incompatible capability; it never silently reports an immutable mismatch. Tokens are scoped to each input document; there are no cross-record identity comparisons. Compiled defaults cannot contain instance tokens. Tokens are neither canonical hashes nor persistent identities, and provide no authorization proof. They are omitted from canonical output. Array entries preserve nested tokens.
